name: Roper Technologies
key_signal: ROP trades 36% below its 52-week high with forward P/E collapsed to 15.2x (vs. trailing 22.7x), pricing in far less growth than the 59% trailing earnings growth and 11.3% revenue growth would suggest, while a fresh 21-day momentum surge (+10.5%) and positive MACD hint the derating is stabilizing.
thesis: Roper's high-margin, recurring-revenue software/industrial model (69% gross margin, 27% operating margin) continues to grow revenue at 11%+ with earnings growth of nearly 60%, yet the stock has been repriced from a premium multiple down to a forward P/E of just 15x — cheap for a serial compounder with this margin profile. The stock is below its 200-day average and golden-cross is negative, but the 21-day momentum (+10.5%) and rising MACD histogram (0.89) suggest the multiple compression is finding a floor and buyers are stepping back in. With only 16 analysts covering a $36.7B large-cap, mispricing from macro-driven multiple compression (rather than fundamental deterioration, given margins and growth are intact) can persist long enough to offer a reasonable entry, and low beta (0.75) suggests the drawdown was sentiment/rate-driven rather than earnings-driven.
bear_case: The 36% drawdown from the 52-week high and persistent negative 126-day momentum (-11.8%) despite the recent bounce could reflect a genuine deceleration in Roper's core software/vertical-market businesses (e.g., insurance software, network software segments) rather than mere multiple compression, and ROE of just 9% alongside elevated debt-to-equity of 55.6% suggests the M&A-driven growth engine is becoming less efficient and more balance-sheet dependent; if forward earnings estimates (justifying the 15x forward P/E) get revised down as growth normalizes from the unusually high 59% earnings growth print, the stock could re-rate lower rather than recover toward its prior premium multiple, especially with price still below both the 50-day (337) and 200-day (388) moving averages on a longer-term basis.
